clues: This city in northeast Egypt runs along the Mediterranean coast. It hugs the west bank at the north mouth of a famed canal.
Though it sits in hot desert land, winds off the sea soften its heat each day. Summers stay less fierce, and winters stay mild and wet.
This city was first built in 1859, at the same time as the great canal it still stands by today. The canal work gave it life.
Wait at its docks long enough, a famed writer claimed, and in time you will meet a friend who roams the world. Folk still tell the tale.
Rows of old houses line its streets, and each floor wears a grand balcony. Their fine fronts give the whole place a look of its own.
